title: OKR-aligned release-train harmonizer and capacity escrow playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a lightweight playbook and tooling spec that coordinates weekly release-train windows across runtime, console, and API teams while aligning launches to Q2 OKRs. The deliverable will: 1) define lane ownership mapped to OKR priorities, 2) formalize a capacity escrow process (reserve/minimum tokens of dedicated capacity and escalation rules), 3) provide a short checklist for cross-team preflight (metrics, canary plan, rollback triggers), and 4) specify a small telemetry dashboard for launch-day health (error budget burn, regional latency spikes, request queuing). The goal is to reduce ad-hoc cutover risk for model-impacting runtime and console releases and give PMs a predictable way to trade off launch timing vs OKR priority.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page playbook document published in Confluence with lane ownership and escalation path
Capacity escrow workflow implemented as a templated ticket for capacity reservations and approvals
A minimal Grafana dashboard created with three widgets: tokenized capacity, error budget burn rate, cross-service 95th latency
A runbook for rollback and emergency deallocation that has been validated in a tabletop rehearsal
notes: Scope limited to launch coordination (not infra provisioning). Any changes touching autoscaler internals will require separate ENG RFC.
We will pilot with two launches in April (console feature flag rollout + runtime quantization rollout).
Use existing billing-backed reservations for Dedicated as the enforced escrow mechanism; for Hosted we will rely on regional fallback policies.
